speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; please state exactly what you were doing immediately before you lost consciousness and how long you remained unconscious. Do you recall any shaking, tongue biting, or incontinence during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio cordis (or arrhythmia triggered by micturition syncope/post-micturition shock). The key features—sudden loss of consciousness immediately after urination, rapid return of consciousness within 30 seconds, and lack of post-ictal confusion—strongly suggest a cardiovascular etiology rather than a seizure. Has he experienced any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath leading up to the event? REQUEST TEST: ECG; REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram; REQUEST IMAGES: ECG_trace.
